Metro Time Helper: Taipei MRT

Support

Everything you need to get around Taipei on time, plus answers to the questions we hear most.

How to use it

  1. Three modes

    Metro Journey Planner works out when to leave for any journey across the network. Xiaobitan shows the Qizhang and Xiaobitan branch timetable and countdown. Beitou · Xinbeitou does the same for the Xinbeitou branch. The app opens in Metro Journey Planner unless you change it.

  2. Switching modes

    Tap the round glass button in the top corner of the screen, the one showing the current mode, then pick the mode you want.

  3. Planning a journey

    Choose a start and a destination from the list or by tapping stations on the map, then pick Arrive by and set the time. The result shows when to enter the station and each leg of the journey. Under Adjust estimate you can choose Standard, which allows half a headway for waiting, or Cautious, which allows a full headway, and set a gate buffer of up to 15 minutes for walking in and reaching the platform.

  4. Departure reminders

    On a branch timetable, set how many minutes ahead you want to be alerted, anywhere from 1 to 30, then tap the train you want. In Metro Journey Planner you can set a reminder for when it is time to leave. Tap an active reminder to cancel it.

  5. Choosing the page it opens on

    Open Settings with the gear button and go to Page on launch. Pick Metro Journey Planner, Xiaobitan, or Beitou · Xinbeitou.

  6. Changing the language

    The app follows your iPhone language by default and offers 50 languages. To use a different one only in this app, open Settings, tap Language, and pick one from the list, or choose Same as system to go back.

Frequently asked questions

  • Why are the times estimates?

    For journeys across the network, the app calculates from Taipei Metro's official headways and station-to-station run times. It does not receive live train positions, so it cannot see delays, crowding, or service changes on the day. Leave yourself some slack for important journeys, use Cautious mode, and always follow station announcements and signs.

  • Where do the branch timetables come from?

    The Xiaobitan and Xinbeitou branches run on fixed timetables published by Taipei Metro, and the app uses those exact departure times, separately for weekdays and weekends. The effective date of each timetable is shown under About in Settings, and you can open the original timetable PDF from the branch screen. If the operator publishes a new timetable, we update it in an app update.

  • I am not getting reminders

    The first time you set a reminder, iOS asks for permission to send notifications. If you declined, the app shows a prompt you can tap, or you can turn notifications back on in the iOS Settings app under Notifications for this app. Reminders are scheduled on your iPhone, so they work offline, but a Focus mode can still silence them.

  • How do I restore my purchase?

    Open Settings in the app and tap Restore. Make sure you are signed in to the App Store with the same Apple Account you used to buy it. Your unlock also comes back automatically when you reinstall the app or set up a new iPhone with that account.

  • How do the 24-hour trial and the unlock work?

    Start the trial from inside the app whenever you are ready, and every feature is open for 24 hours. The trial is recorded by the App Store, so reinstalling does not restart it. When it ends, you can still see the app, and a one-time purchase unlocks everything for good. It is not a subscription and never renews. The price is shown in the App Store in your local currency.

  • Which lines are covered?

    Wenhu, Tamsui-Xinyi with the Xinbeitou branch, Songshan-Xindian with the Xiaobitan branch, Zhonghe-Xinlu, Bannan, and the first phase of the Circular line. The Taoyuan Airport MRT and light rail lines are not included.

  • Is this an official Taipei Metro app?

    No. Metro Time Helper is an independent app and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation. It uses Taipei Metro's official public data. For service disruptions or lost property, please contact the operator directly.

Contact us

Questions, a timetable that looks wrong, or an idea for the app? Write to us. Mentioning your iPhone model, iOS version, the app version (shown in Settings), and the stations involved helps us look into it faster.
